title: Throughput fuzz & surface probing for mixed-arrival continuous-batching runtime
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Goal: Build and run a probing harness that fuzzes arrival-rate mixes and sequence-length distributions to map the throughput vs. latency surface for our continuous-batching runtime. We want to identify operating regions where token/sec is maximized without p95 latency regressions, surface unexpected queue amplification, and produce deterministic triggers for automated regression detection.

Scope: workload synthesis (arrival profiles + length histograms), runtime flags sweep (batch size caps, batch timeout, KV cache hot-prefix rate), and telemetry extraction (tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, queue length distributions, batch composition). Deliverables: harness code, data pipelines to Grafana/Parquet, a canonical throughput-latency surface visualization, and a candidate regression rule set for CI alerts.

result_summary: Initial runs show two distinct failure modes: (1) microburst mixes with high short-sequence ratio cause underfilled batches and sharp p95 inflation when batch_timeout is high; (2) bimodal arrivals with interleaved long sequences cause KV cache churn leading to throughput loss (~15-25%). The throughput-latency surface reveals ridges where small config tweaks (lower timeout, aggressive prefix caching) recover tokens/sec but may worsen p50 for long sequences. The regression detector prototype flags the staging regression reliably across 3 reproducible runs.
next_steps: 1) Land scheduler mitigation in ENG-96301 and re-run sweep; 2) Finalize canonical profiles (short-heavy, bursty, bimodal) and publish seed bank; 3) Wire regression detector into PR checks with a noise-tolerant sliding window; 4) Produce a runbook for interpreting surface visualizations and recommended knob sets for Dedicated vs Hosted tiers.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoffs considered: lowering batch_timeout recovers throughput for bursty clients but increases scheduling overhead for long sequences; raising batch_size_cap helps amortize kernel startup cost but increases tail latency for low-concurrency tenants. We prioritized minimizing customer-visible p95 regressions for Hosted rather than absolute tokens/sec for Dedicated where customers may accept higher tail latencies for throughput.
